main_text.l: Inde aliquanto tempore finc usurpatione regali sufceptas partes procuraverunt, {a} Arrideo[?] quodam Philippo Alexandri fratre regnate, cui perimbecillo verbo datum imperium videbatur: res autè penes eos erat, qui sibi exercitum & provincias distribuerant. Nec vero hic rerum status diu manfit, omne[?]q; se reges appellari malu- erunt. Primus in Syria post Alexandrū Seleucus rex fuit, subjecta eidem Perside ac Babylone. Qua tempestate Iudæi annuum stipendium trecenta argenti talenta regi dabant: nec tamen per {b}ternos magistratus; sed per sacerdotes suos regebantur, patrioque ritu vivebant. Donec ple-rique eorum longa rursum pace corru-pti, miscere omnia seditionibus & turbare coeperunt, affectantes summum sacerdotium libidine, avaritia & dominan-di cupidine. Namque primum sub rege Seleuco, Antiochi magni filio, Oniam sacerdotem, virum sanctum atque inte-grum, Simon quidam falsis apud regem criminibus infimulatum, {c}exquirere ne quiverat. Interiecto deinde tempore, la-son frater Oniae,{d} Antiochum regem, qui Seleuco fratri successerat, adiit, augmen-
{a} Arideo: the marginal note above, as printed beside line 2.

page.notes: Several marginal notes are hyphenated across lines and are copied as printed. Marked uncertain: "Arrideo", "omne[?]q;" (the word after omne is damaged), "bexter" and "Sig.", and "Epiphā" with its abbreviation. The printed "Donec ple-rique eorum" shows a possible spacing gap ("riqueeorum") that is transcribed as "rique eorum". The mark "{a}" before "Arideo" and the mark "{b}" before "ternos" are read from the scan as "*a" and "b". The "{c}" and "{d}" marks stand for the printed letters c and d. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout. The printed word "giftratus" is read as "magistratus" after the hyphen "ma-". The last line ends with "augmen-" and the continuation is not printed on this page.
